# KKT — Kitty Kat Technologies

> Business-first data & AI delivery for mid-enterprise companies in traditional, asset-heavy industries — oil & gas, energy, retail, fuel retail, logistics. Based in Tallinn, Estonia (EU). We start from the business question, not the technology, and ship solutions that run in real operations. Marquee deployment: Optimus, in pilot at Red Petroleum — a 250-station independent fuel network in Kyrgyzstan.

Kitty Kat Technologies OÜ (public brand: KKT) is a data, AI, and automation delivery firm registered in Tallinn, Estonia. It works with mid-enterprise companies — roughly $100M–$1B in revenue — that have established operations, legacy systems, and complex processes, where the cost of getting things wrong is real and the value of a working solution is measurable. Domain expertise and technical delivery sit in one team, so an engagement runs from the business question to a solution that operates in production.

Every engagement that KKT accepts starts with a fixed two-week diagnostic: kick-off, investigation, and synthesis, ending in a readout. Delivery is held together by senior PMO discipline — scope, sequencing, and ownership — and follows a four-stage arc from a business question to a system that keeps running without KKT. Strong AI capability is treated as the baseline; the rigor is in the programme management around it.

The flagship product is Optimus — a procurement-and-margin engine for fuel networks. It turns buying from a decision made on experience and availability into one made on data: demand forecast, the right volume and moment, honest supplier comparison, and the full landed cost of a batch. Optimus is in pilot at Red Petroleum, a 250-station independent fuel network in Kyrgyzstan. It is one embodiment of KKT's broader fuel work, which spans the whole network economy — procurement and margin, logistics, stations and shops, customers, finance and control — built bottom-up, connected data and control first, then AI where it earns its place.

KKT avoids vendor-hype language. Outcomes are stated in measurable terms — margin, cash, availability, customer value, productivity — or not stated at all. The firm is candid about poor fit: it declines pure strategy without delivery, engagements with no senior internal owner, and full outsourcing.

- [Optimus](https://kittykat.tech/solutions/optimus/): The product page. Optimus is the procurement-and-margin engine for fuel networks — one embodiment of KKT's fuel work; in pilot at Red Petroleum.
- [Fuel retail](https://kittykat.tech/industries/fuel-retail/): The fuel positioning — connected data first, AI on built foundations, bottom-up across the whole network economy. Optimus is one embodiment.
- [Retail](https://kittykat.tech/industries/retail/): Mid-enterprise retailer starting points. Links to the open Retail AI Canvas playbook.
- [Case studies](https://kittykat.tech/case-studies/): Named client engagements, expanded in place. Includes Red Petroleum (fuel retail, Kyrgyzstan — 250-station network, Optimus in pilot for procurement and margin), Click & Grow (B2C smart indoor gardens — customer analytics and ML segmentation for Eastern Europe / CIS), GTE (industrial compressor manufacturer — finance/manufacturing reporting plus ML for anomaly detection and energy-consumption optimisation), Kricon (international logistics — operational visibility, anomaly detection, clustering), CSC Telecom (mid-sized telecom — customer and product analytics), Taxigo, Clubtek, a major TIC company, and smaller engagements.
- [Insights](https://kittykat.tech/insights/): A working-in-public column from named authors at KKT.
